reference_drawer.title: 📖 Trig Ratios Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Fundamental trigonometric ratios and right-triangle relationships.

items.rule: Sine, cosine and tangent are side ratios relative to a chosen acute angle.
items.example: In a 3-4-5 triangle, choose the reference angle before assigning sides.

items.rule: The hypotenuse square equals the sum of the squares of the legs.
items.example: Use the positive square root for a side length.

items.rule: Cosecant, secant and cotangent are reciprocals.
The acute angles of a right triangle are complementary.
From a·cotθ=b, isolate cotθ before rewriting the requested expression.
items.example: Then tanθ is the reciprocal of cotθ.

concepts.title: 1. Trigonometric Ratios
concepts.subtitle: Opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse
concepts.summary: For an acute angle in a right triangle, sine is opposite/hypotenuse, cosine is adjacent/hypotenuse and tangent is opposite/adjacent. Reciprocal functions give cosecant, secant and cotangent.
